nc-sbe-2026-candidate-listing.title: Candidate Listing 2026 (Candidate_Listing_2026.csv): the March 3 primary and the November 3 general election, county by county
nc-sbe-2026-candidate-listing.note: The SHA-256 is the whole CSV's as fetched (8288 rows, every office); only the kept cells of the State Senate, State House, Supreme Court and Court of Appeals rows are saved. Columns taken by name: election_dt, county_name, contest_name, name_on_ballot, party_contest, party_candidate, has_primary, is_unexpired, vote_for; addresses, telephones, e-mail and filing dates are never read. The rows dated 11/03/2026 are the November ballot; every county's list of a contest agrees, and the counties a district reaches are those whose rows carry it. The list gives no ballot order and no status column (a candidate who withdraws is taken out of the file). The rows dated 03/03/2026 were used to check the primary results: every candidate agrees. The district attorney, superior court and district court contests on the same list are read with the local contests (nc-sbe-2026-candidate-listing-local).

nc-sbe-2026-primary-results.agency: North Carolina State Board of Elections
nc-sbe-2026-primary-results.title: Precinct results, March 3, 2026 primary election (results_pct_20260303.zip)
nc-sbe-2026-primary-results.note: State Senate, State House and Court of Appeals primaries summed over every precinct (administrative precincts included) by county, then statewide; each row's four voting methods add to its total. The results carry no write-in line for these contests, so a field's total is the sum of its candidates' votes. Every candidate's statewide sum equals the results site's official total.

nc-sbe-2026-primary-enr.agency: North Carolina State Board of Elections
nc-sbe-2026-primary-enr.title: Election results site: 03/03/2026 OFFICIAL PRIMARY ELECTION RESULTS - STATEWIDE
nc-sbe-2026-primary-enr.note: Control only (from https://er.ncsbe.gov/?election_dt=03/03/2026): every county and the state are titled OFFICIAL, with 2633 of 2633 precincts reporting; the statewide totals match the precinct file exactly. The site lists no election between March 3 and November 3, 2026, so no second primary was held. Kept fields only.

nc-openstates-roster.title: Sitting North Carolina legislators
nc-openstates-roster.note: Who holds each seat today and which candidate is the sitting member (same chamber and district, the name fits, one fit only); names, party and ids only. The roster carries no judges.

nc-sbe-2026-candidate-listing-local.agency: North Carolina State Board of Elections
nc-sbe-2026-candidate-listing-local.title: Candidate Listing 2026 (Candidate_Listing_2026.csv): the November 3 general election's county, school, soil and water, municipal, sanitary district, district attorney and trial court contests, county by county
nc-sbe-2026-candidate-listing-local.note: The SHA-256 is the whole CSV's as fetched (8,288 rows, every office, both elections). Of its 4,527 rows dated 11/03/2026, 725 are federal (left to the federal pages), 1,378 are the State Senate, State House and appellate court rows (nc-sbe-2026-candidate-listing) and 2,424 are read here: one row for each candidate on each county board's ballot. Columns taken by name: election_dt, county_name, contest_name, name_on_ballot, party_candidate, is_partisan, is_unexpired, vote_for; the name parts, street address, city, state, ZIP code, telephones, e-mail and filing date columns are never read, and only the kept cells are saved. Every county board's list of a contest agrees, name for name and in the same order: the 2,424 rows placed are 2,118 candidacies in 1,135 contests, each row in exactly one. The list gives no ballot order and no status column (a candidate who withdraws is taken out of the file), and it has a row only for candidates, so an office nobody filed for is not in it.

nc-census-2020-place-codes.title: 2020 place codes, North Carolina (st37_nc_place2020.txt)
nc-census-2020-place-codes.note: Names and five-digit place codes of North Carolina's 553 incorporated cities, towns and villages. Each municipality on the candidate list is the one place of the same name (68 of 68 matched); the file holds no personal details.

nc-sbe-candidate-lists-page.agency: North Carolina State Board of Elections
nc-sbe-candidate-lists-page.title: Candidate Lists (web page)
nc-sbe-candidate-lists-page.note: Read only for whether it says the November candidate lists are final; the finding and the page's SHA-256 are kept, not the page, which links the list files and carries no candidate details. It said the November lists were not yet final, because some local contests had not yet filed.

local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026, of North Carolina's 100 counties, all 100 elect a sheriff, all 100 a clerk of superior court, 99 county commissioners and 24 a register of deeds; soil and water conservation district supervisors, district attorneys and superior and district court judges are on the same ballot (G.S. 163-1, 139-6). Cities, towns, villages and sanitary districts hold their regular elections in odd-numbered years (G.S. 163-279, 130A-50), next in 2027; the 68 municipalities and 10 sanitary districts on this list vote in even years instead. The general law elects county boards of education at the March primary (G.S. 115C-37); the list has November contests for boards of education in 82 counties.
local_calendar.s: N.C. General Statutes 163-1, 163-279, 139-6, 115C-37 and 130A-50 (N.C. General Assembly); counts from the State Board of Elections' Candidate Listing 2026

local_coverage.t: Loaded from the State Board of Elections' candidate list as read on September 30, 2026: every November 3 contest in it for county offices, boards of education, soil and water conservation districts, cities, towns and villages, sanitary districts, district attorneys and superior and district court judges, 1,135 contests and 2,118 candidates, with a local contest in all 100 counties. The list states no ballot order, has a row only for candidates (an office nobody filed for is not in it) and no mark for anyone who withdrew; ballot questions, write-in candidates and local primaries are not loaded. On September 30, 2026 the Board's page said its November lists were not yet final.
local_coverage.s: North Carolina State Board of Elections, Candidate Listing 2026 (Candidate_Listing_2026.csv)

gaps.w: local contests added to the list after it was read
gaps.r: On September 30, 2026 the State Board of Elections' candidate-lists page said its November lists were not yet final, because some local contests had not yet filed and the Green Party could still name candidates; this loader reads the Board's list again each time it runs.
The State Board of Elections' candidate list has a row for each candidate, so an office that drew no candidate does not appear in it; a county's own sample ballot is the place to check for one.
